CHIEF COMPLAINT: Right-sided low back/buttock pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: This 47-year-old female presents with a 14-month history of right-sided pain localized just below the L5 level, over the posterior sacroiliac region, non-radiating. She denies any preceding trauma. She has undergone a structured trial of conservative care over the past 8 months including scheduled NSAIDs and a trial of duloxetine for pain modulation, a home activity modification program limiting prolonged sitting and asymmetric loading, and 12 weeks of formal physical therapy focused on core stabilization and SI joint-specific exercises. Despite this, she continues to report persistent pain rated 7/10 that limits her ability to work as a retail associate.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: Hypertension, controlled. No history of inflammatory disease. No fibromyalgia or somatoform disorder; psychiatric review of systems is negative and she has no diffuse tender points on exam.

PHYSICAL EXAM: Palpation reveals focal tenderness directly over the right posterior SIJ with no comparable tenderness at the greater trochanter, lumbar paraspinals, or coccyx. Lumbar range of motion is full and non-painful. Provocative testing: thigh thrust test positive on the right; Gaenslen's test positive on the right; Patrick's (FABER) sign positive on the right. Distraction test negative. Hip range of motion is full and pain-free bilaterally.

IMAGING: Plain radiographs of the right hip obtained in clinic show no evidence of osteoarthritis or other bony abnormality. MRI of the lumbar spine performed last month shows mild disc desiccation at L4-5 without significant canal or foraminal stenosis and no nerve root impingement correlating with her symptoms.

DIAGNOSTIC INJECTIONS: Patient underwent fluoroscopically guided, contrast-confirmed right SIJ injection with local anesthetic and corticosteroid six weeks ago, with the patient reporting 90% relief of her pain for approximately 6 hours post-procedure, consistent with the expected duration of the anesthetic. A repeat image-guided contrast-enhanced injection performed two weeks later again produced approximately 80% relief for a similar duration.

ASSESSMENT: Findings are consistent with right sacroiliac joint dysfunction as the primary pain generator, refractory to prolonged conservative management, confirmed by two concordant diagnostic blocks.

PLAN: Discussed percutaneous minimally invasive SIJ fusion as next step given failure of extensive non-operative care and positive confirmatory injections. Will obtain preoperative labs and schedule procedure. Continue current PT program in the interim.
